hints: Identify the total number of roses ($5 + 3 + 2 = 10$) and note that there are only $2$ white roses available.
Determine all possible values for the random variable $W$, representing the number of white roses in a selection of $3$: $W \in \{0, 1, 2\}$.
Calculate each probability without replacement, multiplying conditional probabilities along the branches and accounting for the order of selections.
Present the results in a probability distribution table and confirm that $\sum \mathrm{P}(W = w) = 1$.
walkthrough:
Determine the sample space and the range of values for the discrete random variable $W$:
There are $5$ yellow, $3$ red, and $2$ white roses, giving $10$ roses in total ($8$ non-white and $2$ white). Martin chooses $3$ roses without replacement. Since there are only $2$ white roses in the shop, the number of white roses chosen can only be:
$$W \in \{0, 1, 2\}$$

Calculate $\mathrm{P}(W = 0)$, the probability of choosing zero white roses (three non-white roses):
$$\mathrm{P}(W = 0) = \frac{8}{10} \times \frac{7}{9} \times \frac{6}{8} = \frac{336}{720} = \frac{42}{90} \quad \left(=\frac{7}{15}\right)$$

Calculate $\mathrm{P}(W = 1)$, the probability of choosing exactly one white rose and two non-white roses:
The white rose can be chosen first, second, or third, giving $3$ mutually exclusive orders:
$$\mathrm{P}(W = 1) = 3 \times \left(\frac{2}{10} \times \frac{8}{9} \times \frac{7}{8}\right) = 3 \times \frac{112}{720} = \frac{336}{720} = \frac{42}{90} \quad \left(=\frac{7}{15}\right)$$

Calculate $\mathrm{P}(W = 2)$, the probability of choosing exactly two white roses and one non-white rose:
The non-white rose can be chosen first, second, or third, giving $3$ mutually exclusive orders:
$$\mathrm{P}(W = 2) = 3 \times \left(\frac{2}{10} \times \frac{1}{9} \times \frac{8}{8}\right) = 3 \times \frac{16}{720} = \frac{48}{720} = \frac{6}{90} \quad \left(=\frac{1}{15}\right)$$

Set up the probability distribution table and verify that the sum of the probabilities equals $1$:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline w & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ \hline \mathrm{P}(W = w) & \frac{42}{90} & \frac{42}{90} & \frac{6}{90} \\ \hline \end{array}$$
$$\sum \mathrm{P}(W = w) = \frac{42}{90} + \frac{42}{90} + \frac{6}{90} = \frac{90}{90} = 1$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Count the total number of rose bushes: 2 white + 3 red + 4 yellow = 9 bushes. We choose 3 bushes without replacement, so the total number of ways to pick any 3 bushes is:
$$\text{Total ways} = \binom{9}{3} = \frac{9 \times 8 \times 7}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 84$$

Find the probability of picking zero white roses ($W = 0$). All 3 bushes must come from the 7 non-white bushes:
$$\mathrm{P}(W = 0) = \frac{\binom{2}{0} \times \binom{7}{3}}{84} = \frac{1 \times 35}{84} = \frac{35}{84} = \frac{5}{12}$$

Find the probability of picking exactly one white rose ($W = 1$). We pick 1 from the 2 white bushes and 2 from the 7 non-white bushes:
$$\mathrm{P}(W = 1) = \frac{\binom{2}{1} \times \binom{7}{2}}{84} = \frac{2 \times 21}{84} = \frac{42}{84} = \frac{1}{2}$$

Find the probability of picking two white roses ($W = 2$). We pick both white bushes and 1 from the 7 non-white bushes:
$$\mathrm{P}(W = 2) = \frac{\binom{2}{2} \times \binom{7}{1}}{84} = \frac{1 \times 7}{84} = \frac{7}{84} = \frac{1}{12}$$

Check that your probabilities sum to 1 to be completely sure of your distribution table:
$$\frac{5}{12} + \frac{6}{12} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{12}{12} = 1$$
